01

Database design · ETL · Google Looker Studio · AWS · QuickSight

All data shown is dummy. The screenshots show design, not results.

CSAT & Experience reporting: data model, ETL and dashboard

I designed the database, built the ETL and designed the dashboard in Google Looker Studio for a customer-satisfaction reporting product, taking survey responses all the way to something stakeholders can act on.

  1. Survey dataMTM survey, one cycle per half-year
  2. ETLPrepare each cycle for reporting
  3. Data modelCycle · category · sentiment · theme
  4. Looker StudioScorecard, insights, trends

Database design

  • Structured the data around the questions the dashboard has to answer: score by category, by survey cycle, against target.
  • Made category, sentiment and theme first-class dimensions, so any view can be sliced and compared without reprocessing.

ETL

  • Built the pipeline that takes each survey cycle from raw responses to reporting-ready tables.
  • Produces what the dashboard reads: category CSAT scores, the positive / neutral / negative split, and counted themes.

Dashboard design

  • Built in Google Looker Studio, leading with one number, overall CSAT against the OKR, so status reads in a second.
  • Filters for date range, category and half-year, then an insights panel written as Observation → Trend → Action.
  • Charts with the target drawn in, then ranked themes per category so every score has a visible driver.

03

QlikSense · Snowflake · ETL · ERDs · A/B testing

Only the Cross Sell dashboard is shown, with row-level data cropped out.

QlikSense dashboards for ExCo and sales, on a Snowflake ETL I built

As a Data Analyst at Singlife, I built the QlikSense dashboards that the executive committee, the partnership distribution team and the cross-sell team worked from, and engineered the Snowflake ETL behind them.

~30% → <4%gap between OpCo and ops/finance numbers
14sheets in the Partnership Distribution dashboard
90%less manual intervention in ETL

OpCo dashboard

  • The executive committee's view of business performance had drifted from operations and finance reporting.
  • Traced how each team produced APE and VNB, found the source of the difference and fixed it.
  • Cut the gap from ~30% to under 4%, added a sheet reporting the true delta, and replaced "black box" dashboard code with a better source data model.
  • Gave senior leadership a shared view of which differences between reporting channels are acceptable.

Partnership Distribution dashboard

  • Automated the partnership distribution team's monthly reporting, which had been done by hand.
  • Built the data model linking the source data to QlikSense, and converted the existing reports into 14 sheets, from branch and adviser performance to conversion rate and top cases per BDM.
  • Saved hundreds of man-hours.

Cross Sell dashboard

  • Built during Singlife's M&A with Aviva, so the cross-sell team and ExCo could read the results of an A/B test and decide on test strategy.
  • Showed age distribution, test and control groups, campaign code and status, plus APE and VNB generated.
  • Let the team track the test through the experiment and helped ExCo pick the best model for the business.

Behind all of it: ETL on Snowflake, documented with detailed ERDs, which cut manual intervention by 90% and saved 50+ man-hours a month.

Marketing intelligence dashboards for a regional e-commerce leader

As a Senior Analyst on the Marketing Intelligence team, I owned two dashboards that leadership and livestream teams used day to day, and ran the weekly business review against GMV targets.

~30%boost in key livestream metrics
+2%Consideration score growth over 1 year

Built on FBI, Lazada's proprietary BI platform. I developed and maintained both dashboards there.

Brand health tracking

Built for the CMO, to read the results of brand health tracking studies at a glance.

FBI · Lazada's proprietary BI platform
  1. Country filterSwitch between our 6 regional ventures, so local and regional CMOs each get their own view.
  2. Auto-written summaryPlain-English headlines on how each metric moved. Rule-based SQL on temporary tables runs on the backend every time the dashboard refreshes.
  3. Brand funnelThe last 3 months of the funnel, shown next to our main competitor's to expose gaps in consumer behaviour.
  4. Funnel by age groupThe same funnel split by the 2 age groups we were targeting at the time.
  5. Daily active usersDAU, pulled from Alibaba's cloud-based SQL servers.
  6. Consideration scoreThe share of respondents who would consider shopping on Lazada. Charted on its own as the headline measure of marketing performance.

Livestream

Built for the livestream lead, to report on performance and judge changes to mechanics and content. The existing dashboard lacked visuals, so I built a visual layer on top of it.

FBI · Lazada's proprietary BI platform
  1. Links to existing docsIt sits on top of the existing data, so it links back to the original documentation and dashboards.
  2. Page views (PV)Times a livestream was opened. This and the metrics below are split by day of the week, as each day has its own theme or series.
  3. Unique views (UV)Unique customers who opened a livestream. Backs up PV, which inflates when people leave and re-enter.
  4. Add-to-cart (A2C)Items added to cart from a livestream. A proxy for sales captured, since shoppers are encouraged to check out only in sale periods, to save more.
  5. Browsing depth (IPVUV)Products viewed per customer in a livestream, or individual page views per unique viewer.
  6. Raw dataSession-level data with filters such as date range and livestream code, so the team can explore without downloading the full dataset each time.

Also: post-campaign analytics that shaped later marketing efforts and KPI setting.
